![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14274266/assets/1083b3341f9ee7105c3df7dbcf896ab89e6afcfbe3bc9a4ec837d24df8b4dd8f.png)

The function $f(x)$ is defined and differentiable on $[-2,7].$ The graph of ${f}^{′}(x),$ the derivative of $f(x),$ is shown above, where the areas of the regions between the graph and the $x$-axis are $6,$ $9,$ and $4,$ respectively (from left to right). Find the minimum value of $f(x)$ on the interval $[-2,7]$ given that $f(-2)=1.$

${f}_{\text{min}}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
According to the candidates' test, the minimum value of $f(x)$ on $[-2,7]$ must occur at a critical point or an endpoint of the interval.

**Step 1**: Find the critical points:

We see that ${f}^{′}(x)$ is defined everywhere on $x\in (-2,7),$ and ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ at $x=1$ and $x=4.$ Therefore, the candidates are $x=-2,1,4,7.$

**Step 2**: Compute the values of $f$ for each candidate using the fundamental theorem of calculus:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) & =1 \\ f(1) & =f(-2)+{\int }_{-2}^{1}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =1-6 \\  & =-5 \\ f(4) & =f(-2)+{\int }_{-2}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =1-6+9 \\  & =4 \\ f(7) & =f(-2)+{\int }_{-2}^{7}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =1-6+9-4 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Select the smallest value of $f$ from our candidates.

Comparing the values of $f$ found in step $2,$ we have 

$$
{f}_{\text{min}}=min\{1,-5,4,0\}=-5.
$$

Therefore, the minimum value of $f$ is ${f}_{\text{min}}=-5,$ and the value of $x$ that minimizes $f(x)$ is ${x}_{\text{min}}=1.$
